purpose: RISC-V debug transport module: a JTAG TAP (state machine, 5-bit instruction register, IDCODE/BYPASS/DTMCS/DMI data registers) that turns host scans on jtag_tdi_i/jtag_tms_i/jtag_tck_i into debug-module-interface read/write requests on dmi_req_o. It returns the response data from dmi_rsp_i and the DTM status on jtag_tdo_o, and lets the host clear a DMI error (dmireset) or block the interface (dmihardreset) through dtmcs.

conceptual_assets.name: CA1 debug command sent to the debug module (address, write data, operation)

C.why: The capture word packs addr, rdata and err but not wdata (L229), so the written data is never shifted back out on TDO; the address is echoed but carries no secret.

I.why: L266-269 copy address, write data and op straight from the host-shifted tap_reg.dmi; the only check is that op is a read or write code (L268); L283-285 present the values to the debug module unchanged.

A.why: A command is accepted only while busy = 0 (L264) and dmihardreset = 0 (L265); an update arriving while busy is discarded and only flagged (L258-259); busy clears only on dmi_rsp_i.ack (L275-276).

U.why: The whole acceptance condition is dmihardreset = 0, the update pulse and ireg = addr_dmi_c (L265); there is no authentication, lock or privilege term anywhere in the module, so any agent driving the JTAG pins issues arbitrary reads and writes.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: An attacker on the JTAG pins shifts a chosen word into tap_reg.dmi (L196); at the next update pulse L266-269 copy it into dmi_ctrl.addr/wdata/op and L283-285 present it as a read or write of any 7-bit debug-module address, with nothing in this module able to refuse it.

conceptual_assets.name: CA2 debug read data returned to the host

C.why: L274 latches dmi_rsp_i.data into dmi_ctrl.rdata, L229 packs it into the capture word, L189 captures it, L209 shifts it out on jtag_tdo_o. rdata is cleared only by rstn_i (L242), not by dmireset/dmihardreset (L248-257), so the last value read stays capturable by any later DMI scan until a system reset.

I.why: L274 follows dmi_rsp_i.data on every busy cycle, not only on ack; the capture at L189 is not gated by busy and the status bits come only from err (L229), so a scan captured during a pending transaction returns an unfinished rdata marked as success (err = 0). replicate_f is not defined in this source; its 2-bit width follows from L65.

A.why: The read completes only when dmi_rsp_i.ack = 1 (L275-276); there is no timeout or abort, so a withheld ack means the read never finishes.

U.why: Capture (L189) and shift-out (L209) depend only on ireg and TAP state; no access condition limits who reads the response.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Any JTAG host that selects addr_dmi_c captures dmi_ctrl.rdata through L229/L189 and reads it on jtag_tdo_o at L209, including a value left by an earlier debug session because L242 is the only clear.

conceptual_assets.name: CA3 DMI transaction state (busy)

C.why: busy is not in the dtmcs capture (L219-226) or the DMI capture (L229); it is never exported.

I.why: busy = 0 is the condition for loading a new addr/wdata/op (L264-269) and for clearing reset requests (L250-252); busy = 1 routes a new update to the drop-and-flag path (L258-259) and enables rdata capture (L274). A busy forced to 0 mid-transaction lets a new command overwrite dmi_ctrl.addr/wdata while L284-285 keep presenting them to the debug module.

A.why: Only dmi_rsp_i.ack (L275-276) or rstn_i (L237) clear busy; the reset requests at L248-252 never assign it, so a missing ack disables the whole DMI path until a system reset.

U.why: No mode overrides busy; the reset requests are themselves held while busy = 1 (L250). The missing abort is recorded under A.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A debug module (or a fault) that never raises dmi_rsp_i.ack leaves busy at 1 (L275-276), so L264 refuses every later command and dmihardreset cannot recover it; forcing busy to 0 instead lets L266-267 overwrite the address and data of a transaction still in flight.

conceptual_assets.name: CA4 DMI reset control (dmireset, dmihardreset) written through dtmcs

C.why: Both bits are reported back in dtmcs by design (L220-221); nothing secret.

I.why: On an update with ireg = addr_dtmcs_c, L248-249 copy dtmcs bits 16/17 into dmireset/dmihardreset; either one clears err (L256-257), and dmihardreset = 1 makes L265 refuse commands.

A.why: While dmihardreset = 1 no command is accepted (L265); it is 1 out of reset (L239) and a host-set value is held for the whole of a busy transaction (L250-251).

U.why: The reset bits are an override that wipes err (L257), the only record that a command was dropped (L258-259).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Setting dtmcs bit 17 or 16 (L248-249) erases the sticky error at L257, so a command dropped at L258 is no longer reported to the host, and bit 17 makes L265 refuse commands for as long as it is held.

conceptual_assets.name: CA5 DMI error status (err, reported as dmistat and as the DMI op field)

C.why: Status bits exported by design (L224, L229).

I.why: err is set when a DMI update arrives while busy and the command is discarded (L258-259); it is the only evidence the host gets of the drop (exported at L229 and L224). A forced 0 reports a dropped write as done; a forced 1 marks every result as failed.

A.why: err does not gate command acceptance: L265 has no err term.

U.why: Because L265 ignores err, later commands keep executing after one was dropped, so the host command sequence runs with a gap until it reads the status.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Clearing err (L257) or preventing L259 hides that a command was dropped, so the host believes a debug write took effect when it did not.

conceptual_assets.name: CA6 selected TAP instruction (ireg)

C.why: ireg is shifted out on TDO during IR_SHIFT by design (L204).

I.why: ireg alone decides which data register a scan captures, shifts and drives to TDO (L186, L193, L206), and whether an update changes the DMI reset controls (L247) or issues a DMI command (L258, L265). A corrupted ireg turns a scan meant for IDCODE or BYPASS into a DMI command or reset.

A.why: LOGIC_RESET and IR_CAPTURE reload a fixed value (L178-179); no separate blocking mechanism beyond I.

U.why: The decode at L186/L193 and the tests at L247/L265 accept addr_dtmcs_c and addr_dmi_c with no lock or unlock condition.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Whoever sets ireg = addr_dmi_c (L181) routes the next DR scan into tap_reg.dmi (L196) and, on update, into a DMI command (L265-269).

hypotheses: IDCODE (L187, L207) reveals version, part and manufacturer to any host. This is the purpose of IDCODE and nothing here makes it secret; it matters only if device identity is treated as sensitive.
The debug module behind dmi_req_o may or may not check authentication. That check is outside this source. If it does not, CA1 gives full debug control of the SoC to anyone holding the JTAG pins.
dmi_ctrl.wdata stays on dmi_req_o.data after the write (L284; cleared only at L243). This matters only if another agent can observe the DMI request bus.

TCK and TMS are sampled by clk_i through three-flop synchronizers (L99-111). A glitch that fakes a TCK edge could step the state machine into DR_UPDATE and fire a command from whatever sits in tap_reg.dmi. This is a fault-injection concern with no mechanism in this module to confirm or deny it.
The field widths of dmi_rsp_i.data and dmi_req_o.*, and the codes dmi_req_rd_c, dmi_req_wr_c and dmi_req_nop_c, come from a package that is not in the pack. I assumed widths from dmi_ctrl (L83-84).

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing all 42 elements (13 ports incl. record fields, 29 signals incl. record fields). The data and control edges gave the paths of 9 flows without reading every line. Reciprocity and id checks all passed: 0 text mismatches over 403 occurrences, 0 unresolved ids, 0 edges without a reverse. Missing edges were the most useful evidence. There is no ack edge on dmi_ctrl.rdata. No reset request ever assigns busy. err gates nothing. dmi_nxt has no edge from wdata.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: Branch polarity: GATES does not say whether the gate is =0/=1 or the else branch (for example busy at L264 gates addr on 0 and rdata on 1). Cycle timing: the one-clock update pulse, op as a one-cycle strobe (L263), dmihardreset reset-to-1 then cleared. Bit-slice meaning: which bits of tap_reg.dmi become addr, data or op (only in the occurrence text). Constants, generics and package items: addr_*_c, dmi_req_*_c, replicate_f, the IDCODE generics, the record types. The absence of any authentication. This had to be read as the full condition at L265, not from an edge. What the debug module does with the request, which is outside the module.
map_assessment.errors_found: No wrong edges found in a full read of every relationship against its line. One inconsistency: the record port dmi_req_o is listed as drive "undriven" while all three of its fields are driven (L283-285). The functionality hints matched the source for every element I checked.

process_notes: 1. Read the prompt, then the whole VHDL (one entity, about 200 lines). 2. Indexed the map with Python: listed elements, storage and counts, dumped every relationship with resolved lines to work/debug_dtm/elements.txt, and read it in full. 3. Ran check_map.py: occurrence text against source, line coverage, id resolution, edge reciprocity. All clean. 4. Named 9 flows from the ports and state: command, read-out, reset request, status, handshake, instruction, IDCODE, bypass, TAP control. Traced each from source to sink on map edges and confirmed each edge on its line. 5. Asked the four questions per value with a line each, giving 6 conceptual assets. IDCODE and bypass got four no answers. 6. Assigned roles. An element is primary if it holds, sets, computes or exports an asset value. It is secondary if it only forwards, or decides when a value moves. Clock and TCK-derived enables were excluded. Where the map changed a decision: (a) dmi_ctrl.rdata has no GATED_BY ack edge. Reading L274 showed rdata tracks the bus every busy cycle, which is the mid-transaction readout finding (CA2 I). (b) No edge from dmireset/dmihardreset to busy means no abort path. That made busy an availability asset (CA3). (c) err gates nothing, so commands continue after a drop (CA5 U). (d) tap_reg.dmi_nxt has no wdata source, so write data is never read back (CA1 C = no). (e) tap_reg.idcode feeds only itself and TDO, and its only non-reset driver is a constant, so it was excluded. Read from source rather than the map: branch polarities (L250, L264, L273), the L265 acceptance condition as a whole, the slice layout (L266-269, L219-229), and the reset value of dmihardreset (L239).
